findings.claim: Loop 2 made test 25 reject a correct, page-modelled call with a message that contradicts the code. reviews-auth-forward now takes the outgoing call to be the first call whose own argument text contains API_BASE_URL (outgoingCall, tests/lab.mjs lines 311-322). It then looks for the forwarded header only in that call or in an httpx.Client (lines 324-334 and 343). The service-to-service page's own example passes a url variable: "await client.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=limits)" (service-to-service-calls/artifact.md line 25). A learner who builds the URL on the line before the call therefore gets no call, and test 25 fails with "send the incoming authorization value on as the outgoing Authorization header of the call to the shop api" (line 343). That message names the header, which is already forwarded, so the learner has no way to find the real cause. Reproduced on scratch copies under the critic workspace with the lab exported at HEAD 607eea16 (lab files equal afe3e48c), npm ci in tests, Node v24.2.0 and LAB_PROJECT; the critic wrote its own 26/26 solution and applied one-change variants to it; no private overlay was read. Moving the f-string into a local url passed to httpx.get fails only test 25 with that message, both with a named header dict and with a dict literal in the call; tests 24 and 26 still pass. Loop 1's rule matched the header text anywhere, so this is new in loop 2. It costs reruns against the four-rerun allowance (ops-edu-r1-04).
findings.recommendation: Locate the outgoing call as the httpx request (httpx.get/post/request or a client method) or as a call whose URL argument is a name assigned from text containing API_BASE_URL. Add the url-variable form, with a named dict and with a dict literal, to the must-pass cases. Keep every ops-edu-r1-02 must-fail case failing. When no outgoing call is found, say that instead of naming the header. Grader and message change only.

findings.claim: Loop 2's 401-guard recogniser rejects two correct forms with messages that contradict the code. It accepts only an if line before the call that tests the missing case (not authorization, is None, == None), and the HTTPException's first argument must be 401 (RAISE_401, tests/lab.mjs line 335; guards, lines 346-352). (a) raise HTTPException(detail=..., status_code=401) in the guard fails test 25 with "your missing-token check does not raise HTTPException with 401" (line 352). handlers() in the same file reads the status keyword in any order (line 364). (b) A positive check that wraps the call, if authorization: or if authorization is not None:, with the 401 raised in the else branch, fails with "a request with no token would reach the shop api without one: answer 401 before the call" (line 350), although it answers 401 and never calls. Loop 1's guard check accepted (b). The ops-edu-r1-02 acceptance did not list it as a must-pass, so this is a regression rather than a reopened acceptance. Reproduced on the critic's solution with LAB_PROJECT; each variant fails only test 25. Likelihood is low: README phase 4 rule 1 (line 80) reads as guard-first, and FastAPI convention puts status_code first.
findings.recommendation: Read the 401 with the same any-order pattern handlers() uses. Accept a positive authorization check whose else branch raises 401 when the outgoing call sits inside the if branch. Keep all five ops-edu-r1-02 must-fail variants failing. Grader change only.

findings.claim: Loop 2 reworded the uvicorn branch of test 23 to "uvicorn without --host uses its default address: reread the adding-FastAPI page ..." (tests/lab.mjs line 205). It prints that for any host other than 0.0.0.0, including an explicit loopback. Reproduced: CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "8000"] fails test 23 with that message, which tells the learner they left out --host when they wrote it. The fastapi branch names the host it was given (line 201), and loop 1's uvicorn message made no such claim. This is off the README path (phase 3, line 74, asks for the page's command), so few learners see it.
findings.recommendation: When hostOf returns a value, print the same message the fastapi branch does ("the server is told to listen on <host>: ..."), and keep the "without --host" wording for the case where no host is given. Message change only.
